verses.zh: （大卫的诗，交与伶长。）愚顽人心里说：没有　神。他们都是邪恶，行了可憎恶的事；没有一个人行善。
verses.en: For the music director, by David.Fools say to themselves,[NOTE:1] “There is no God.”[NOTE:2] They sin and commit evil deeds;[NOTE:3] none of them does what is right.[NOTE:4]
notes: Psalm 14. The psalmist observes that the human race is morally corrupt. Evildoers oppress God’s people, but the psalmist is confident of God’s protection and anticipates a day when God will vindicate Israel.
Heb “a fool says in his heart.” The singular is used here in a collective or representative sense; the typical fool is envisioned.

“There is no God.” The statement is probably not a philosophical assertion that God does not exist, but rather a confident affirmation that God is unconcerned about how men live morally and ethically (see Ps 10:4, 11).

Heb “they act corruptly, they make a deed evil.” The verbs describe the typical behavior of the wicked. The subject of the plural verbs is “sons of man” (v. 2). The entire human race is characterized by sinful behavior. This practical atheism—living as if there is no God who will hold them accountable for their actions—makes them fools, for one of the earmarks of folly is to fail to anticipate the long range consequences of one’s behavior.

verses.zh: 耶和华从天上垂看世人，要看有明白的没有，有寻求　神的没有。
verses.en: The Lord looks down from heaven[NOTE:1] at the human race,[NOTE:2] to see if there is anyone who is wise[NOTE:3] and seeks God.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “there is none that does good.”
The picture of the Lord looking down from heaven draws attention to his sovereignty over the world.
Heb “upon the sons of man.”
Or “acts wisely.” The Hiphil is exhibitive.

verses.zh: 他们都偏离正路，一同变为污秽；并没有行善的，连一个也没有。
verses.en: Everyone rejects God;[NOTE:1] they are all morally corrupt.[NOTE:2] None of them does what is right,[NOTE:3] not even one.
notes: Anyone who is wise and seeks God refers to the person who seeks to have a relationship with God by obeying and worshiping him.
Heb “everyone turns aside.”
Heb “together they are corrupt.”

verses.zh: 作孽的都没有知识吗？他们吞吃我的百姓，如同吃饭一样，并不求告耶和华。
verses.en: All those who behave wickedly[NOTE:1] do not understand—[NOTE:2] those who devour my people as if they were eating breadand do not call out to the Lord.
notes: Heb “there is none that does good.”
Heb “all the workers of wickedness.” See Pss 5:5; 6:8.

verses.zh: 他们在那里大大地害怕，因为　神在义人的族类中。
verses.en: They are absolutely terrified,[NOTE:1] for God defends the godly.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “Do they not understand?” The rhetorical question (rendered in the translation as a positive affirmation) expresses the psalmist’s amazement at their apparent lack of understanding. This may refer to their lack of moral understanding, but it more likely refers to their failure to anticipate God’s defense of his people (see vv. 5-7).

Heb “there they are afraid [with] fear.” The perfect verbal form is probably used in a rhetorical manner; the psalmist describes the future demise of the oppressors as if it were already occurring. The adverb שָׁם (sham, “there”) is also used here for dramatic effect, as the psalmist envisions the wicked standing in fear at a spot that is this vivid in his imagination (BDB 1027 s.v.). The cognate accusative following the verb emphasizes the degree of their terror.

verses.zh: 你们叫困苦人的谋算变为羞辱；然而耶和华是他的避难所。
verses.en: You want to humiliate the oppressed,[NOTE:1] even though[NOTE:2] the Lord is their[NOTE:3] shelter.
notes: Heb “for God is with a godly generation.” The Hebrew noun דּוֹר (dor, “generation”) refers here to the general class of people who are characterized by godliness. See BDB 190 s.v. for other examples where “generation” refers to a class of people.

Heb “the counsel of the oppressed you put to shame.” Using a second person plural verb form, the psalmist addresses the wicked. Since the context indicates their attempt to harm the godly will be thwarted, the imperfect should be taken in a subjunctive (cf. NASB, NRSV) rather than an indicative manner (cf. NIV). Here it probably expresses their desire or intent (“want to humiliate”).
It is unlikely that כִּי (ki) has a causal force here. The translation assumes a concessive force; another option is to understand an asseverative use (“certainly, indeed”).

verses.zh: 但愿以色列的救恩从锡安而出。耶和华救回他被掳的子民那时，雅各要快乐，以色列要欢喜。
verses.en: I wish the deliverance[NOTE:1] of Israel would come from Zion!When the Lord restores the well-being of his people,[NOTE:2] may Jacob rejoice,[NOTE:3] may Israel be happy![NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “his.” The antecedent of the singular pronoun is the singular form עָנִי (ʿani, “oppressed”) in the preceding line. The singular is collective or representative here (and thus translated as plural, “they”).
The deliverance of Israel. This refers metonymically to God, the one who lives in Zion and provides deliverance for Israel.
Heb “turns with a turning [toward] his people.” The Hebrew term שְׁבוּת (shevut) is apparently a cognate accusative of שׁוּב (shuv).
The verb form is jussive.

PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary which means
that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of
us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are
priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3).
Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above.
Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original
author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has
one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: PSALM 14:1-3
1The
fool has said in his heart, "There
is no God."
They are
corrupt, they have committed abominable deeds;
There is no one who does good.
2The Lord
has looked down from heaven upon the sons of men
To see if there are any who
understand,
Who seek after
God.
3They have
all turned aside, together they have become corrupt;
There is no one who does good, not
even one.

14:1 "fool" This psalm is almost
exactly like Psalm 53. This word (BDB 614 I) refers to people who should
know YHWH but choose to live as if He does not affect their lives. There
were no atheists in the philosophical sense in the ANE, but many of the
covenant people were practical atheists (cf. Deut. 32:6,21; 2 Sam. 13:13;
Ps. 10:4,11,13; 53:1; 74:22; Ezek. 13:3). The proverb of Luke 12:48 surely
applies to these people.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FOOLISH PEOPLE

▣ Notice how "the fool" is characterized.

- they are corrupt ‒ BDB 1007, KB 1469, Hiphil PERFECT
(i.e., a settled condition)

- they have committed abominable deeds ‒ BDB 1073, KB 1765, Hiphil
PERFECT (i.e., a settled condition)

▣ "There is no God" This is the recurrent falsehood propogated by
the wicked (cf. Ps. 10:4; 14:1; 36:1). There is no deity to judge their motives and/or
actions. This is the essence of a "fool."

▣ "abominable deeds" See
Special Topic below.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ABOMINATION (OT)

▣ "There is no one who does good"
This is a general statement on the spiritual condition of fallen mankind,
even the covenant people. It is elaborated on in Ps. 14:2-3. Notice how
fallen humanity is characterized.

- no one does good, Ps. 14:1,3 (inclusive)

- no one understands

- no one seeks after God

- all have turned aside (see note at Ps. 14:3)

- all have become corrupt

One clearly sees the influence of Genesis 3 on all humanity. Paul put
together a powerful litany of verses on human rebellion in Rom. 3:9-18,23.
He quotes Ps. 14:1-3; 53:1-4; 5:9; 140:3; 10:7; Isa. 59:7-8; Ps. 36:1.
This truth is the first truth of the gospel (Rom. 1:18-3:18). The gospel
is "good news" in light of the bad news!

14:2 "The Lord has
looked down from heaven" YHWH was believed to dwell in
heaven, from which He sees and knows all that occurs on earth (acts,
motives, intents, cf. Ps. 33:13,14; 102:19; Job 28:24). YHWH, so different
from the idols, sees, knows, and acts (cf. Gen. 11:5; 18:21; Exod. 2:25; 3:7)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HEAVENS AND THE THIRD HEAVEN

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANTHROPOMORPHIC LANGUAGE TO DESCRIBE GOD

14:3 "they have turned aside" This VERB
(BDB 693, KB 747, Qal PERFECT) denotes a settled
action. YHWH's covenant was a clearly-marked path/road/way. His people were to
stay on this straight (i.e., righteous) and narrow road, but they did not
(cf. Exod. 32:8; Deut. 9:12; 11:16; 17:11,17; Jdgs. 2:17; 1 Sam. 12:20; 2
Kgs. 22:2; Jer. 5:23; 17:13; 32:40). The turning away was not an act of
ignorance but purposeful rebellion!

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY

▣ "not even one" This is very emphatic! See Paul's comment
in Rom. 3:10-18,23.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALL OF MANKIND

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: PSALM 14:4-6
4Do
all the workers of wickedness not know,
Who
eat up my people as they eat bread,
And do not call upon the
Lord?
5There
they are in great dread,
For
God is with the righteous generation.
6You
would put to shame the counsel of the afflicted,
But the Lord
is his refuge.

14:4-6 This strophe heightens the results of "not knowing" (BDB 393, KB 390,
Qal PERFECT). The VERB "know" can denote
an intimate, personal relationship, not just facts. The actions of the wicked against the poor,
needy, and those with no social voice or power will be judged by God,
their protector (cf. Deut. 10:17-19; 14:29; 24:17,19-22; 26:12,13; 27:19)!

He is their "refuge" (BDB 340, cf. Ps. 2:12; 5:11; 34:22). To
attack them is to attack Him. He will defend them.

SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW

SPECIAL TOPIC: REFUGE

14:4

NASB, NKJV, NRSV, LXX
"do not call upon the Lord"

TEV
"they never pray to me"

NJB, REB
"they never call to YHWH"

JPSOA
"do not invoke the Lord"

The VERB (BDB 894, KB 1128, Qal PERFECT)
is a common one used in many ways (i.e., a wide semantic field). In Psalms it has several usages.

- of priests in ritual and prayer ‒ Ps. 99:6

- of the prayers of the covenant people ‒ Ps. 4:3; 20:9;
50:15; 86:5; 91:15; 107:6,13; 116:2; 141:1

- the nations do not call on YHWH (i.e., Ps. 79:6; the NASB 1970, wrongly
translates this as Adon, but in the MT it is YHWH) but Israel does
‒ Ps. 14:4; 50:15; 53:4

In the NT this OT worship phrase (i.e., ritual and prayer) becomes a way
of denoting entrance into a relationship with YHWH through Jesus (cf. Acts
2:21; 22:16; Rom. 10:9-13).

We are a called people who call on the name of the Lord and are then
called to service! Prayerlessness is a sign of false faith and practical
atheism!

SPECIAL TOPIC: CALL ON THE NAME

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE NAME OF THE LORD (NT)

14:5 "There they are in great dread"
Literally this is "they feared a fear" (Qal PERFECT
and NOUN of the same root; BDB 808, KB 922).

Since "there" is undefined, some switch it to the end of the
phrase and add "where there is no fear" (AB, NJB).

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: PSALM 14:7
7O,
that the salvation of Israel would come out of Zion!
When the Lord
restores His captive people,
Jacob
will rejoice, Israel will be glad.

14:7 "O, that the salvation of Israel"
This is a title for YHWH who dwells in Zion (i.e., Mt. Moriah, the
temple). Notice the parallel of "YHWH" in line 2.

This verse is also found in Ps. 53:6, which means it may be proverbial.
The LXX makes this first line a question.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ZION

SPECIAL TOPIC: SALVATION (OT term)

▣ "restores" This same VERB
(BDB 996, KB 1427) also can mean "repent" or "turn back."
However, in this context Israel is not called on to repent.

There is a word play between "restores" (BDB 996) and "fortunes"
(BDB 986). The footnote in the NET Bible has "turns with a turning
(toward) his people" (see v. 5b, YHWH is with His people).

▣ "Jacob. . .Israel" The
Patriarch Jacob had twelve children who became the thirteen tribes (Joseph's
two sons were both adopted by Jacob). Jacob's
name was changed to Israel in Gen. 32:22-32.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ISRAEL (THE NAME)

▣ "restores His captive people" One could interpret this phrase as

- released from exile

- released from the domination of evil people

This Psalm seens to look back to Genesis 3; 10-11, but also
refers to the national conflicts that the nation of Israel faced.

▣ "rejoice. . .be glad" Both
of these VERBS denote the result of
restoration. VERBS in Hebrew take their time
orientation from the context. This context is future.

- rejoice ‒ BDB 162, KB 189, Qal JUSSIVE

- be glad ‒ BDB 970, KB 1333, Qal IMPERFECT
used in a JUSSIVE sense

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means
that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of
us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are
priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the
major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be
thought-provoking, not definitive.

- What did the fool mean by his statement, "There is no God"?

- Does the OT teach that all humans are sinful?

- What does it mean "to call upon the Lord"?

- Does Ps. 14:7 imply an exile?
